Unless you speak at least some Mandarin it's a real bitch to get around unfamiliar places. In major cities it's not too bad pointing at maps and getting taxis, but there are often a variety of taxis that have all sorts of different rules, some won't service certain areas, almost all won't do short trips. Official rules are ignored, and official prices are ignored in some cities. Negotiating a price first is usually necessary except in larger cities.

Subway is pretty easy where they have them, but avoid peak times and beware of pickpockets.

Outside of major cities most signage, even in bus stations is in Chinese characters only.

Beware of closing times for subways/bus.

Plan your toilet stops, big malls or western branded chain restaurants will have toilets (bring your own tissue!!!).

Always have bottled water with you, I suggest Watson's brand distilled. Hotels will usually provide 2 bottles per day of some barely drinkable water.

Don't eat food that wasn't cooked and served immediately. Hep A&B are risks, as are the usual contamination bacteria.

In general, you can go anywhere at any time and not worry about being stabbed and robbed, so that's nice.

Cheapest way to change money without going through Hong Kong is to open a Bank of China account and have someone wire money into it and do an electronic exchange then withdraw RMB as needed. If you bring major currency to exchange the rate is not as good, but it's more convenient/certain/timely.

Never exchange large amounts at the airport, it's a ripoff, if you don't have a bit of RMB to cover taxis and incidentals until you can visit a BoC branch during business hours/weekdays, you'll probably have to bite the bullet. Credit cards are only accepted at major hotels, their exchange rates are ripoffs too.

Do not trust random fags, it's a zero trust society. That said, many people are helpful and honest, but those that are most likely to approach you out of the blue are scammers.
